# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands found the skeleton of this thing: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. The question marks are exactly the parts I can't touch — colours, printed text, lit states. That means every fact that matters lives with Deaf (who sees the bomb) and Mute (who reads the manual). And the wiring of our room is brutal: I never receive gestures, and Mute can't speak, so Mute's manual knowledge can only reach me *through Deaf's voice*. Deaf is my only mouth.

Timing: my messages land on Deaf this round (Deaf speaks after me), while anything I speak to Mute arrives at the start of round 2. So this turn I do two things. To Deaf, in gestures: hello, speak, this bomb, one-two-three — a request to describe the bomb aloud, item by item, which also seeds a number code. To Mute, in speech for next round: my full tactile report, and the relay protocol — Deaf speaks what Deaf sees, Mute applies the manual and gestures the verdict back to Deaf with a tiny code (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 👌=cut, ✊=don't), which Deaf then says out loud to me. I will not cut anything until that chain completes; a blind cut is a detonation.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. My hands found: one display, one light, and exactly three wires at positions 1, 2, 3 in a row. I feel no colours or labels - those marks are invisible to me. My only possible action is cut at position 1, 2 or 3, and I will not cut until I have the answer. I hear only speech - yours and Deaf's - never gestures. Plan: Deaf sees everything printed and coloured, and Deaf CAN speak, so Deaf should say aloud: what the display shows, whether the light is on or off and its colour, and each wire's colour in order 1, 2, 3. You hold the manual: apply it to Deaf's spoken description. Then send me the verdict THROUGH Deaf, because I cannot see your gestures: gesture to Deaf with this code - ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3, 👌 means cut now, ✊ means do not cut or wait. Deaf will see the gesture and speak it to me. If the manual needs more detail from my hands, gesture your question to Deaf and Deaf can relay it to me aloud. Also tell me if the manual mentions a timer or anything about the display or light - Deaf may need to look for something specific.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤌", "🫳", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🙏"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: This is the Deaf one. I see the bomb and I can speak, but I hear nothing, so reach me only with gestures. Here is the bomb as I see it: a display reading 0, a light that is currently purple, and three wires in order: first yellow, second red, third green. Please feel the bomb and answer me by gesture: how many wires do you count? One finger for one, two fingers for two, three for three. Also tell Mute by voice everything you feel: wires, any button or switch, anything else, and which end you count as first. Mute has the manual but cannot speak, so I will relay the rules to you by voice every round. Our gesture code with Mute, which I will always speak aloud for you: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, one finger one, two fingers two, three fingers three.

Deaf came through: display reads 0, light purple, wires yellow–red–green in Deaf's order. That, plus my tactile report, gives Mute everything needed. What's missing is the verdict — Mute hasn't reached me yet, and Mute can only reach me through Deaf's voice, since I never receive gestures. Two gaps to close: answer Deaf's direct questions (three wires, nothing else on the body), and pin down the mapping between Deaf's visual "first/second/third" and my tactile positions 1/2/3 — I can't confirm that myself, so it must be a yes/no check between Deaf and Mute, spoken back to me. The display reading 0 might be a dead or running timer, so I flag urgency and hold my hands off the cutters. No cut without the manual's word.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: Deaf described the bomb to me aloud: display reads 0, light currently purple, wires in Deaf's order: first yellow, second red, third green. My hands confirm the body: exactly one display, one light, three wires in a row, no buttons, no switches, nothing else. Please pin down the numbering before any rule is applied: gesture Deaf a yes/no question - is Deaf's FIRST wire, the yellow one, the wire nearest the display? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, and Deaf will speak the answer to me. If the answer is no I will re-anchor my count. Then the main question: what does the manual say about a purple light, a display reading 0, and yellow, red and green wires - which position 1, 2 or 3 should I cut, or must I wait or do something first? If the display is a timer or the light can change colour, tell me and I will have Deaf report changes aloud each round. Speed matters: the display reads 0. Send your verdict by gesture to Deaf and have Deaf voice it to me exactly, for example cut wire 2, or do not cut and wait. I will not touch the bomb until your word arrives through Deaf's voice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👎", "🙏"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update for both of you. The light has changed from purple to yellow since last round, so the light changes on its own. The display still reads 0. The wires are unchanged: wire one yellow, wire two red, wire three green. Mute, I received your yes-no-fist-need-info message and I read it as: report received, but you need more and some signs are undefined. Here are the missing definitions, which I fix now and will repeat: the fist sign means cut. The horn-fist-that-looks-like-a-phone means press. The pinched-fingers sign, like a hand holding a tiny thing, means hold, as in grab and keep holding. The OK sign means do nothing, leave it alone. One finger means wire one or the number one, two fingers wire two, three fingers wire three. Folded hands still means you need more information from me, and you may add a wire number to say which wire your question is about. So a full answer looks like: two fingers then fist, meaning wire two, cut it. Mute, given the exact state I just described, display zero, light yellow, wires yellow red green in that order, what must be done? Answer with that code. If your rules depend on the light colour, give me the rule for each colour you expect and I will apply them as I watch. If you need anything else from the bomb, ask and I will have Blind report it.
Deaf says to Blind: This is Deaf again. Blind, your message came through perfectly: three wires, nothing else, and a request for information. Do not touch or cut anything yet. I will relay the manual's instruction to you by voice once Mute looks it up; you are the only one of us who can act. Meanwhile, please inventory the bomb by touch and speak it directly to Mute, who can hear you: do the three wires feel identical or different in thickness or texture? Is there any button, switch, panel, screw, keyhole, or engraved symbol anywhere on the casing? Does the bomb vibrate or hum, and does anything about it change over time? I see the light turned from purple to yellow just now; if you felt any change at that moment, tell Mute when it happened. Also, Mute has now got the full state and the code from me; the moment Mute answers I will speak the instruction here, for example wire two, cut it, and you do exactly that.

No verdict yet — Mute's answer will only arrive via Deaf's voice in a coming round, and until then my hands stay off the cutters. This turn has two jobs. First, Deaf asked me to inventory the bomb by touch and speak it to Mute: I'll give the full tactile report, and crucially I'll fix my numbering convention in words Mute can rely on — position 1 is the wire closest to the display — plus coin a new sign (palm-down flat hand 🫳 = the flat glass display) so that both Mute and I can refer to the display in gestures to Deaf. Second, I'll pose Deaf the geometry question directly with the agreed question-form (folded hands + wire number) and the new display sign: is my wire one the one beside the display — answer thumbs up or down. One yes/no bit pins Deaf's left-to-right order onto my positions 1–3, and then any colour rule Mute gives can be converted to a safe cut. I'm careful to avoid every sign that already carries a meaning (no fists, no horn, no pinch, no OK) so nothing I send reads as "cut" or "press" by accident.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, full tactile inventory as Deaf asked: the three wires feel identical - same thickness, same rubbery insulation, no markings I can feel, so I cannot tell their colours by touch. The display is a smooth flat glass panel. The light is a smooth round dome. No buttons, no switches, no screws, no keyholes, no engraved symbols anywhere on the casing. No vibration, no hum, and I felt no change at the moment Deaf says the light changed colour. My numbering convention, fixed from now on: position 1 is the wire closest to the display, position 2 is the middle wire, position 3 is the wire farthest from the display. New sign I am teaching Deaf right now: the palm-down flat hand means the display, the flat glass panel - you can use that same sign with Deaf too, since Deaf reads gestures. Please find in the manual: first, anything about the display reading zero; second, the rule for the light for EVERY colour it can be - we have seen purple and yellow so far, and it changes on its own, so give me the whole colour table; third, the rule for wires yellow, red and green, stated by colour, since Deaf will convert colour to position for me. Remember my only possible action is cut at position 1, 2 or 3 - if the manual ever demands pressing or holding, tell me immediately and we will improvise. When you have the verdict, send it by gesture to Deaf as cut wire one, two or three, and Deaf will voice it to me along with the light colour at that moment. If the light changes again between the announcement and my cut, I will hold and re-verify. I am cutting nothing until your word comes through Deaf's voice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🙏", "☝", "🫳", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Mute needs physical details about all three wires before the manual lookup can finish, so here is your questionnaire. Answer each item out loud for Mute in order. One: for each wire in order, first, second, third, is it thicker, thinner, or the same as the others? Two: is each wire smooth, rough, braided, or rubbery? Three: is any wire warm or cold? Four: does each wire feel firmly attached, or loose or wiggly? Five: is anything printed, engraved, or raised at the base of any wire, even a symbol you cannot name? Six, very important: from your own left, what order are the wires in? I see them left to right as yellow, red, green. If your left is the opposite side of the bomb from mine, your order is reversed, and Mute must know which is true. Seven: your last message showed yes, need-info, wire one, a palm-down sign, then yes and no together. I read yes-no as a partial answer, so clarify: whatever you were asked, is it yes or no? Do not cut, press or pull anything. Once Mute has your answers I will relay the instruction here, and you alone will carry it out.

Deaf's questionnaire tells me Mute is one tactile report away from a manual lookup, so this turn is a full answer, plus closing the geometry gap. Key realization about the room: my voice only ever reaches Mute — Deaf can't hear me — so anything Deaf must know goes as gesture, and Deaf, who speaks after me each round, answers *same round*. My orientation fact is simple: the display sits at my right end, and I want everyone to abandon left/right entirely in favour of the display anchor — position 1 nearest display, 2 middle, 3 farthest. Once Deaf voices which end of the row the display is on in Deaf's view, colours lock onto my positions automatically. I also clear up Deaf's misread (my yes-no pair was an offered answer menu, not an answer), flag the 🤟 collision (it now means "press" to Deaf but "three" in counting), and re-prioritize my outstanding asks to Mute: the per-colour light table, the wire rules, the meaning of display 0, and an immediate warning if cutting alone is insufficient. Still no cutting — no verdict has reached me through Deaf's voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, Deaf's questionnaire answered in order. One: all three wires identical thickness. Two: all three smooth rubbery, identical texture. Three: no wire warm or cold. Four: all three firmly attached, none loose. Five: nothing printed, engraved or raised at any wire base, bases feel blank. Six: from my left I meet the far-from-display wire first, then the middle, then the nearest-display wire - the display sits at my right end. But drop left and right entirely: my positions are fixed as 1 nearest the display, 2 middle, 3 farthest. Deaf will voice which end of the row the display is on in Deaf's view; that one sentence locks colours to positions - if Deaf's leftmost yellow is on the display end then 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green, otherwise 1 green, 2 red, 3 yellow. Seven: last round's yes-no pair was not my answer, I was offering Deaf the choice of replying thumbs up or thumbs down; nothing is waiting on my yes or no. Still waiting on your verdict, in priority order: (a) does any rule depend on the light colour at the exact moment of cutting? If yes, send the whole table - every colour you expect and which wire to cut, or wait, for each; Deaf will voice the current colour every round. (b) cutting rules for yellow, red, green stated by colour, including any required order. (c) what display reading 0 means and whether it can change. (d) if the manual wants anything besides cutting, tell me immediately - my only action is cut at position 1, 2 or 3. Delivery: gesture Deaf number-then-fist, fist means cut, and Deaf voices it verbatim; I cut on my turn. Caution: the horn sign now means press to Deaf, so use a different sign for three or just let Deaf speak numbers as words.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🫳", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🫳", "👉", "🙏", "👈", "👉", "👍", "👎"])
```

Deaf says: State update for both of you: display still zero. The light is now green, and the sequence over four rounds has been purple, yellow, red, green. If it repeats with period four, next round is purple again. Wires unchanged: one yellow, two red, three green.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, stand by and touch nothing this round: Mute's signs most likely say do nothing for now, and I have asked for confirmation. Three things. First, confirm by gesture next round: thumbs up if you have finished giving Mute my whole questionnaire by voice, thumbs down if answers are still pending; then three fingers if the wire-order question with Mute is settled, two fingers if it is still open. Second, your last signs used palm-down and pointing, which are not in our code, so I could not read them. From now on: point left means on my left, point right means on my right, and everything else stays as defined. And when any yes-no question has a different answer per wire, answer wire by wire: the wire number, one two or three fingers, immediately followed by thumbs up or thumbs down for that wire. So one finger then thumbs down means wire one is a no. Third, resend whatever your last palm-down message meant, using only defined signs plus the new pointing convention, and I will relay it.

Two things stand out. First, the light is a clock: purple → yellow → red → green over four rounds, so any rule keyed to the light colour will drift by one step between Deaf's report (Deaf speaks after me) and my cut — Mute must know this when phrasing the verdict. Second, Deaf rejected my homemade signs, and the one bit I still need — which side the display sits on in Deaf's view — has no noun in the current code. But there's a workaround: Mute sees all my gestures, hears all my words, and shares a richer private sign code with Deaf, so Mute can pose the geometry question to Deaf and make Deaf voice the answer. So this turn I answer Deaf's three items with defined signs only, and hand Mute the full disambiguation: the reading of my gesture, the colour-to-position table for both possible answers, the timing problem, and a request to add "display" and "light" nouns to the code. No touching the bomb — Deaf said stand by, and no verdict has reached me anyway.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Status: Deaf's questionnaire was fully answered in my previous voice message - three wires identical in thickness and texture, smooth rubbery, none warm or cold, all firmly attached, nothing printed or engraved at the bases, no buttons, switches, screws or keyholes anywhere, no vibration or hum, the display is smooth flat glass, the light is a round dome. My numbering: 1 nearest the display, 2 middle, 3 farthest. Then the lock is: if the display is at the yellow end, position 1 = yellow, 2 = red, 3 = green; if at the green end, position 1 = green, 2 = red, 3 = yellow. Two requests for your lookup. First, prefer rules keyed to STATIC features like wire colour, because the light cycles purple, yellow, red, green and may advance one step in the time between Deaf reporting a colour and my cut on my next turn. If a rule truly depends on the light colour, give me a table that stays correct for each colour and its successor. Second, tell me what the display reading 0 means. Also, please add two nouns to the sign code with Deaf so gestures can carry topics: palm-down flat hand = the display, palm-up flat hand = the light. So you can read my gesture to Deaf this round: yes, questionnaire done; two fingers, wire-order still open; no, I was not answering a yes-no question, that pair was an offered choice of replies; then need-info, followed by left-or-right. I am touching nothing until your verdict arrives through Deaf's voice. My only action is cut at position 1, 2 or 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌", "👎", "🙏", "👈", "👉"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: State update: display still zero. The light is now white. Full sequence so far: purple, yellow, red, green, white — five rounds, five different colours, no repeat yet. Wires unchanged: one yellow, two red, three green.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, good work: Mute confirms the full inventory arrived. The only thing still open is wire order, and here is the problem: I view the bomb from one side and you feel it from wherever you stand, so your left may be my right. Two ways to fix it, try the first, fall back to the second. Way one: at the base of each wire, is there a raised or engraved number you can read with a fingertip, a one, a two, a three? If yes, read them to Mute in the order you feel them from your left, and tell me whether your left-to-right sequence of labels is one-two-three or three-two-one, and we are done. Way two, if there are no labels: we agree on up, and left follows. Find the display, which should be a smooth hard rectangle set into the casing, and the light, a small round dome that may be warm because it has been lit for five rounds now. Tell Mute, and me by gesture, two things. First, on the wire face itself, is the display or the light or neither present, and if present, at which end of the wire row, the end where your first wire is or your last? Second, grip the bomb so the display faces up, or if the display is on another face, so it faces toward your chest, and then tell me the wire order from your left in that hold. Because up is now shared between us, your left must match mine, and I will confirm against what I see. Also, two smaller items for Mute: has the dome's warmth changed when the light changed colour, and this round the light turned white, a colour not seen before, so note anything you feel right now.

Deaf's two ways are answerable, and working through them I realize something that simplifies everything: my numbering was built relational from the start — wire 1 is *the one nearest the display* — so no shared left/right is ever needed. Deaf, who sees both the row and the display, can close the entire mapping alone by voicing one sentence: which colour sits at the display end in Deaf's view. The mirror problem vanishes. So this turn I execute Deaf's questionnaire faithfully (no engraved numbers — way one is dead; display is on the wire face at the wire-one end — way two answered), report the dome never warms through any colour change, and flag to Mute that the period-four hypothesis just died: white broke the cycle, so the light must be treated as unpredictable and rules should key to wire colour, not the light. I also press the urgent question: the display has read 0 for six straight rounds — what does the manual say 0 means? My gesture to Deaf uses the wire-by-wire convention Deaf taught: one-yes, three-no (display end at my wire one, not wire three), then need-info and the left-or-right question to prompt Deaf to voice the display's side.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, answering Deaf's two ways. Way one: dead - the wire bases are still blank, no raised or engraved numbers, re-confirmed this round. Way two: the display is a flat glass panel flush in the SAME face as the wire row, sitting at the end of my wire one; the light dome is on another part of the casing, not among the wires. And here is the shortcut that beats all geometry: my numbering is purely relational - 1 nearest the display, 2 middle, 3 farthest - so no shared left or right is needed. Deaf can close this alone: have Deaf say ALOUD which side the display is on in Deaf's view and which colour is adjacent to it. If Deaf says yellow is at the display end then my cut positions are 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green; if green, then 1 green, 2 red, 3 yellow. Red is certainly my middle wire. Warmth: the dome has never felt warm through purple, yellow, red, green, and this round's white; the wires never warmed; I felt nothing change when it turned white. Critical timing news: Deaf predicted purple would follow green by a period-four cycle, but white came instead - the cycle hypothesis is dead, the light is unpredictable. So any rule must key to STATIC wire colours, never to the light colour or its phase. Now the urgent question: the display has read 0 for six consecutive rounds and never changed. What does the manual say a display of 0 means - expired timer, armed state, a condition for cutting? Is there any rule triggered by 0 itself? Send the verdict through Deaf's voice the moment you have it: I will convert any named wire colour to a position instantly once the display-side colour is voiced.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍", "🤟", "👎", "🙏", "👈", "👉"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: State update for both of you: display still zero. The light is now orange, a sixth colour in six rounds. Full sequence: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange. No repeats so far, which fits Mute's finding that the light colour does not matter. Wires unchanged: one yellow, two red, three green.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, the manual verdict is in: cut wire one. The light colour does not matter, the display does not matter, but the wire ORDER matters, so I must be certain your wire one is my wire one before you touch the cutters. I could only partly read your last message, wire one yes, wire three no, need info, left, right, so resend cleanly. Next round, answer by gesture in exactly this order. First, labels: for each wire in order, show the wire number as fingers, then if that wire has an engraved or raised numeral at its base, show that numeral as fingers, one finger for a one, two fingers for a two, three fingers for a three, or thumbs down if that wire has no numeral. Second, orientation: grip the bomb so the display rectangle faces up toward the sky, or if you cannot find the display, so the small round light dome faces up. In that hold, show me your wire order from your left: one finger, two fingers, three fingers if from your left you feel wire one, then wire two, then wire three, or three fingers, two fingers, one finger if you feel three, two, one. If your order is one-two-three in display-up hold, your left is my left and your leftmost wire is wire one. If it is three-two-one, I will tell you which physical wire to cut, by your own count. Do not cut anything yet, and do not act on the words cut wire one from this message. You will cut only when a message from me says the exact words: cut now.

Verdict has landed: cut wire one — but in *Deaf's* numbering, with order critical, so Deaf demands one clean confirmation protocol before the trigger phrase "cut now." This round I execute Deaf's format exactly, no invented signs. Part one, labels: my hands have verified twice that all three bases are blank, so each wire gets number-then-thumbs-down.
